messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: CANARY ALERT: service=web-gen route=canary-3 | error_rate=12% (threshold=5%) | p95=1.2s | triggered at 2025-11-04T17:22:47Z. Paging @alice_oncall and oncall escalation. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/internal/canary-3
alice_oncall: Got the page, looking. Anyone seen matching deploys?
claire_prod: We pushed a soft-flag rollout 09:30 PDT to enable new caching layers for gen models. Canary % = 5%. Could be related.
bob_sre: Checking host-level metrics now. Seeing CPU on gpu-node-14 spike + memory kv-cache growth. Attaching small logs here:
```
[2025-11-04T17:21:01Z] request_id=... latency=0.45s status=200
[2025-11-04T17:22:33Z] request_id=... latency=1.15s status=502 model=redwood-2-7b quant=8bit
[2025-11-04T17:22:34Z] request_id=... latency=1.18s status=502
```
dave_engineer: That looks like cache mismatch + OOM fallback on that variant. The new caching change kept more KV entries. If canary traffic holds it'll saturate GPU memory. Recommend flip the flag and drain canary traffic.
alice_oncall: Agreed. First priority is customer impact. Claire, any customer-facing 500s reported yet?
claire_prod: Not in CS queue yet. Internal monitoring shows a small bump in 5xx from a subset of tenants (~3% of traffic), mostly long-context requests. No major user complaints so far.
alice_oncall: OK. Plan: 1) Pause canary traffic routing, 2) Flip feature flag for caching to off for canary, 3) Drain in-flight requests, 4) Verify smoke and metrics, 5) Roll forward fix in staging. Who can run the flag flip and drain?
bob_sre: I can run drain and verify infra. dave, can you flip the flag?
dave_engineer: On it. Flipping feature flag: `flagsctl set gen_cache_v2 canary-3 false --reason "canary spike"`
pagerduty-bot: Incident acknowledged by alice_oncall. Escalation level: SEV3 -> SEV2 due to error rate increase.
claire_prod: Noting customer impact classification: degraded latency + small 5xx rate on niche tenants. Communications hold until rollback completes.
dave_engineer: Flag flip complete. Command run: 
```
$ flagsctl status gen_cache_v2 --env canary-3
gen_cache_v2: disabled (was enabled)
```
bob_sre: Initiating traffic drain for canary route. Command: `routingctl set-weight web-gen canary-3 0 --grace-period 60s`
bob_sre: Drain started. Current active sessions on canary: 28 -> 12 -> 2
alice_oncall: Good. Monitoring error rate and p95.
incident-bot: Canary health: error_rate=3.1% | p95=0.48s after flag flip and drain.
claire_prod: Running smoke tests against primary route and a handful of tenants. No errors observed in 20 runs.
dave_engineer: Also rolled back the canary build to previous artifact as a precaution: `deployctl rollback web-gen canary-3 --to-tag web-gen@rel-2025-11-02`
bob_sre: Backend metrics look stable. GPU memory reclaimed on node-14.
alice_oncall: Nice. Next: verification checklist — (a) error_rate under 1% for 10m, (b) p95 under 600ms for 10m, (c) no new 500s in CS queue, (d) tag rollback verified. Assigning bob_sre to keep watch for 30m and bob to sign off.
bob_sre: Watching. Will post final in 30m.
claire_prod: Filing postmortem ticket and linking the rollback action and flag flip in the ticket.
alice_oncall: Thanks all. Also capture the exact commands used in the incident log. Quick note for postmortem: consider adding a graceful eviction for kv cache or memory limit guard on canary variants.
dave_engineer: Filed GH issue: https://github.com/redwood/inference/issues/8342 — propose cache size limit by model.
incident-bot: Incident updated: status=mitigated | severity lowered to SEV3 | mitigations applied: flag_flip, drain, rollback.
bob_sre: Final check — error_rate=0.8%, p95=0.42s over last 10m. No 500s in CS.
alice_oncall: Marking thread for handoff to post-incident review. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
